segments.text: Coils, relays, connectors and terminal blocks don't have a flat top. A vacuum nozzle can't seal on them, and at high speed the part tilts or drops.
segments.chapter: Why vacuum nozzles fail on odd-form parts

segments.text: Southern Machinery designs and manufactures gripper nozzles for JUKI JM odd-form insertion machines, in our own factory in Shenzhen since 2011.
This is the SM-2070. Over the part, its jaws slide open, up to eleven millimetres.
It descends into the tray pocket. The slim jaws pass the neighbouring parts and reach below the middle of the component.
Then the jaws slide together horizontally. A true parallel clamp, with no scissor tilt.
The head lifts and moves at full speed. The part is held mechanically, so it stays square.
Over the upward camera, the machine checks the part and its leads.
Then the leads go straight into the holes in the PCB.
The jaws open, release the part, and the head returns for the next one.

Two models cover the range. The SM-2070 opens from zero to eleven millimetres, for parts from one to nine point five millimetres. The SM-2071 opens from eight point five to eighteen point five, for parts from nine point five to seventeen point five millimetres. Both have slim, seven by seven millimetre arms.

They plug into the standard tool changer on the JUKI JM-10, JM-20, JM-50 and JM-100, and on KE-2000, FX and RS-1 series machines. We also supply standard JUKI 700-series and 800-series gripper nozzles.
Need a custom design, like our 2723 or 2583 C grippers? Send us your JUKI model, a drawing of the part, and samples or photos. Custom tooling in about seven days. Email info at smthelp dot com.

seo.description:
Coils, relays, connectors and terminal blocks don't have a flat top. A vacuum nozzle can't seal on them, and at high speed the part tilts or drops. Southern Machinery designs and manufactures gripper nozzles for JUKI JM odd-form insertion machines, in our own factory in Shenzhen since 2011.

How the SM-2070 works
• Jaws slide open over the part, up to 11 mm
• Descends into the tray pocket; slim jaws pass neighbouring parts and reach below the component's middle
• Jaws slide together horizontally: a true parallel clamp, no scissor tilt
• Lifts and moves at full speed; the part is held mechanically and stays square
• Upward camera checks the part and its leads
• Leads go straight into the PCB holes
• Jaws open, release, and the head returns for the next part

Two models, one method
• SM-2070: opening 0–11 mm, for parts 1–9.5 mm (Molex / Hirose FPC, TO-220, D-PAK, micro-relays, small pin headers)
• SM-2071: opening 8.5–18.5 mm, for parts 9.5–17.5 mm (Bobina coils, transformers, power relays, terminal blocks, heavy E-caps)
• Both: 7 × 7 mm arms (width × height)

Compatibility
• JUKI JM-10, JM-20, JM-50, JM-100
• JUKI KE-2000 series (KE-2010 to KE-2060), FX-1/2/3, RS-1 series
• Plug and play on the standard tool changer
• We also supply standard JUKI 700-series GA/GB/GC/GD/GE chucks and 800-series Type 800–803 gripper nozzles

Custom gripper nozzles (for example our JUKI A 2723 and 2583 C designs) in about 7 days. Send us:
1. Your JUKI machine model and nozzle station
2. A dimensioned drawing of the part
3. Samples or photos
